channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Benedita da Silva lidera corrida ao Senado no RJ, diz pesquisa
item.description: Benedita da Silva (PT) leads the Senate race in Rio de Janeiro across two scenarios, with 34.2% and 35.9% of voting intentions, respectively. In both cases, the candidates competing for the second seat are in a technical tie due to the 2.4 percentage point margin of error. The survey, conducted by Paraná Pesquisas between June 1–3, 2026, among 1,680 respondents in 62 municipalities, is registered with the TSE under RJ-05645/2026 and cost R$ 45,000 funded by private resources.

item.title: Eduardo Paes lidera no 1º e 2º turnos para o governo do RJ
item.description: The Paraná Pesquisas survey released on June 4, 2026 shows Eduardo Paes (PSD) leading the race for Rio de Janeiro state governor in both rounds: with 48.3% in the first round and 60% in a potential second-round matchup against Douglas Ruas (PL), who has 24.5%. Anthony Garotinho (Republicanos) trails with 9.2% in the first round, technically tied with Ruas given the 2.4-point margin of error. The poll interviewed 1,680 people across 62 municipalities from June 1–3, 2026, and is registered with the TSE under RJ-05645/2026.

item.title: Trump dá ‘presente’ a Lula com novo tarifaço; Flávio Bolsonaro tenta conter danos
item.description: The U.S. proposed 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods, which the Lula government seized as a political opportunity to attack Flávio Bolsonaro, accusing him of seeking U.S. intervention against Brazil’s Pix system and national sovereignty. Lula labeled the Bolsonaros 'traitors' and 'sellouts of the homeland,' using the issue to strengthen his campaign narrative of defending national sovereignty. Petista militants coined 'TARIFLÁVIO' to link the senator to the tariffs, while the Brazilian government formally accused the Bolsonaros of interfering in internal affairs.

item.title: STF é “ruim” ou “péssimo” para 46% dos brasileiros, diz PoderData
item.description: A PoderData poll shows 46% of Brazilians view the STF's performance as 'bad' or 'terrible', down 6 points from 52% two months prior, yet still far above the 15% rating it 'good' or 'excellent'. Negative perception stems from the Court's proactive role in political issues, including the fake news inquiry, and ongoing tensions with Congress, which seeks to limit its powers.

item.title: Juros mais baixos: o que se sabe da linha de crédito para compra de moto por entregadores
item.description: The Lula government is preparing a subsidized credit line for motorcycle delivery workers from apps like iCloud, offering low interest rates and using the FGO as a guarantor fund, requiring at least six months of platform activity. The program aims to finance the purchase of conventional or electric motorcycles, with payments deducted directly from workers’ earnings, targeting 700,000 to 1.2 million informal, low-income workers.

item.title: JK: a verdade dignifica a Nação
item.description: The article argues that Juscelino Kubitschek’s death in 1976 was a planned assassination by the Brazilian military dictatorship, not a traffic accident. It contends that after the regime’s humiliating defeat in the 1974 Senate elections, Kubitschek represented a democratic threat and was targeted for years through multiple failed attempts. The text claims the dictatorship coordinated with Chilean intelligence to eliminate him, and his death sparked a national outpouring of grief and renewed commitment to democracy against authoritarianism.

item.title: Como acabar com o desmatamento e a degradação globais até 2030
item.description: The Roadmap to Halt and Reverse Forest Loss and Degradation by 2030, launched by President Lula at COP30 in Belém in November 2025, aims to coordinate global action among 99% of UN member states to fulfill the Paris Agreement’s mandate. Despite the clear mandate, the initiative risks fragmentation in governance, financing, and negotiations, potentially becoming another unfulfilled catalog of pledges. Its success hinges on defining clear responsibilities, resources, timelines, and metrics to turn intentions into coordinated action.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: Caso Vorcaro leva Flávio a crise de credibilidade e afugenta eleitor independente
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's messages to banker Daniel Vorcaro, requesting funds to finance the film 'Dark Horse', undermined his credibility among independent voters — a decisive bloc in the 2026 election. Qualitative research by Genial/Quaest showed these voters, who had been moving toward Bolsonaro as an alternative to the PT, became undecided or returned to supporting Lula, calling the audio a 'disappointment' and 'shameful'.

item.title:
Quem politizou o
comércio exterior
item.description: The text suggests that the escalation of U.S. tariffs against Brazil is tied to the Bolsonaro family, citing Eduardo Bolsonaro’s social media post thanking Trump after accusations of a political ‘witch hunt’ against Jair Bolsonaro, and a photo of Trump with Flávio Bolsonaro posted between sanction announcements. The PL candidate (likely Jair Bolsonaro) attempts to distance himself from these links, but the article implies strong evidence of the politicization of foreign trade by Bolsonaro allies.

item.title: Ameaça de Trump pode tumultuar eleição, mas não garante vitória a Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Recent moves by the Trump administration in Brazil have stirred the electoral race, but were not primarily aimed at helping Flávio Bolsonaro defeat Lula in October. Trump’s agenda consistently prioritizes his own interests above allies or even U.S. national interests. The article emphasizes that, despite the external disruption, there is no assurance that Trump’s actions will directly benefit Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign.

item.title: A eleição que ninguém vê — e que decide tudo
item.description: The Federal Chamber election, though largely unknown to voters, is pivotal for presidential governability, public fund allocation, and shaping policies in health, education, and pensions. It moves billions of reais and determines whether the president will have legislative support to govern — yet most Brazilians cannot name a single candidate.

item.title: PF e PGR analisam segunda versão de delação de Vorcaro e devem dar resposta nos próximos dias
item.description: Federal police and prosecutors are reviewing a second version of Daniel Vorcaro’s plea bargain proposal after the first was rejected for omissions and lack of genuine cooperation. The new submission includes additional details and more robust accounts, but no decision has been made on acceptance, further requests, or rejection. Vorcaro has changed his legal team to signal cooperation, though investigators previously viewed his conduct as an attempt to delay facing maximum-security imprisonment.

item.title: Planalto avalia que classificação do PCC e do CV como terroristas não deve ter efeito imediato
item.description: The U.S. government has designated Brazil's PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, but the Brazilian Planalto assesses that the effects will not be immediate, anticipating primarily economic impacts such as sanctions on financial institutions and restrictions on information sharing. While Lula's aides fear potential U.S. military operations in Brazil, they consider this scenario unlikely in the short term.

item.title: Prefeitura do Rio anuncia pacote de mais de R$ 22 bilhões em investimentos até 2028
item.description: Rio de Janeiro Mayor Eduardo Cavaliere announced a R$22.1 billion investment package for the city through 2028, funded by federal and private sources. The announcement, made at the Museum of Tomorrow four months ahead of the state election, included completed, ongoing, and planned projects such as the Parque Oeste expansion, bus fleet renewal, and infrastructure and mobility initiatives.

item.title: Lula: “No podemos aceptar el trato de Estados Unidos a Brasil esta semana”
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva harshly criticized U.S. policy under Donald Trump, stating he cannot accept the treatment Brazil received this week. He referenced the threat of new U.S. tariffs and the designation of two Brazilian criminal groups as terrorist organizations. Lula also accused Bolsonaro supporters of treason for encouraging foreign interference.

item.title: Fundo eleitoral 2026: confira como será distribuição dos R$ 4,9 bilhões; PL, PT e União lideram
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) announced the distribution of R$ 4.9 billion from the Electoral Fund for the 2026 elections. The PL leads with R$ 881.7 million, followed by the PT (R$ 615.4 million) and União Brasil (R$ 526.2 million), together accounting for about 40% of the total. The funds are exclusively for campaign financing and require accountability, with gender and race quotas to be defined by each party.

item.title: Flávio afirma que Lula é o “único do Brasil” que quer tarifas dos EUA
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) accused President Lula (PT) of being the 'only person in Brazil' who wants the 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods, claiming Lula provoked the U.S. with aggressive rhetoric against Marco Rubio and argued that dialogue with Trump could avoid the tariffs. Lula countered that Flavio undermined negotiations with Trump and called him a 'traitor to the nation'.

item.title: Trump 'rompe trégua com Lula' e causa 'tempestade' no Brasil: o que disse a imprensa internacional sobre tarifas
item.description: The Financial Times reports that new U.S. measures — including designating Brazilian factions as terrorist organizations and proposing a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods — broke a truce between Lula and Trump, sparking a 'political storm' in Brazil. The newspaper links these actions to lobbying efforts by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who met with Trump at the White House, and says Lula used the tariffs to accuse Flávio of betraying the country, dubbing the policy 'TariFlávio'.

item.title: Nunes Marques assume relatoria de representações eleitorais envolvendo Flávio Bolsonaro e Master no TSE
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques, president of the TSE, assumed rapporteurship of three high-impact electoral representations: one from the PL against AtlasIntel over an allegedly fraudulent poll involving Flávio Bolsonaro, and two from the PT against the film Dark Horse, alleging economic abuse and seeking to suspend its circulation. Nunes Marques also appointed himself as an auxiliary judge for the 2026 elections, alongside Vice President André Mendonça, in a move that deviates from the Court’s usual practice.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro tem “hiperfoco em corrupção”, diz Renan Santos
item.description: Renan Santos, a presidential pre-candidate from the Mission party, stated that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) has a "hyperfocus on corruption," contrasting him with former president Jair Bolsonaro, who, despite involvement in schemes like the "rachadinha," did not exhibit the same obsessive focus on corruption. Renan cited Flávio's ties to Banco Master and negotiations for the financing of the film "Dark Horse" as evidence. Flávio Bolsonaro's team did not respond to requests for comment from Poder360 by the time of publication.

item.title: Apesar de barulho político com nova taxa, Brasil e EUA têm ‘conversa sóbria’ nos bastidores
item.description: Although the announcement of new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian products sparked political noise in Brazil — including mutual accusations between the government and opposition involving Senator Flávio Bolsonaro — diplomatic backchannels indicate that trade negotiations continue in a calmer, more favorable environment than public rhetoric suggests, according to editor Robson Bonin. The government is seeking to politically exploit the timing of the tariffs alongside Flávio Bolsonaro’s recent U.S. visit, while the opposition attempts to blame the Planalto for diplomatic strain, all within the pre-electoral context of 2026.

item.title: PL receberá maior fatia do fundo eleitoral para campanhas do TSE
item.description: The TSE announced it will distribute R$4.9 billion from the Special Campaign Financing Fund to the 30 parties contesting the October 2026 elections. The PL will receive R$881 million, the largest share, followed by the PT with R$615 million and União Brasil with R$526 million. Together, the three parties will receive about 40% of the funds, based on electoral law criteria including Chamber votes, bench size, and Senate representation.

item.title: TSE divulga distribuição de R$ 4,9 bi do Fundo Eleitoral; PL, PT e União ficam com 40% do total
item.description: The TSE announced the distribution of R$ 4.9 billion from the Electoral Fund for the 2026 elections, with PL, PT, and União Brasil collectively receiving about 40% of the total. PL leads with R$ 881.6 million, followed by PT (R$ 615.3 million) and União Brasil (R$ 526.2 million). The allocation follows legal criteria based on party representation in Congress and past electoral performance.

item.title: Trump confirma ida à cúpula do G7 e pode se encontrar com Lula
item.description: Donald Trump confirmed his attendance at the G7 summit in France from June 15–17, 2026, following a UFC event at the White House. He may meet with Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to discuss proposed U.S. additional tariffs on Brazilian imports over alleged forced labor in supply chains. Brazil is not a G7 member but was invited by France, and the meeting remains unconfirmed.

item.title: Decisões recentes de Trump sobre Brasil dificilmente serão revertidas no curto prazo
item.description: Recent U.S. decisions, including labeling PCC and CV as terrorist organizations and imposing tariffs on Brazilian exports, are unlikely to be reversed in the short term, as they stem from a broader Trump foreign policy strategy rather than Brazilian electoral interests alone. Despite Brazilian diplomatic efforts to delay the measures, they were driven by State Department factions led by Marco Rubio and are expected to persist. 2026 candidates must adjust their rhetoric to this new external pressure environment.

item.title: Lula embarca para o G7 em meio à crise com Trump
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva confirmed his attendance at the G7 summit in France from June 15–17, after initially considering skipping the meeting. He decided to participate to defend multilateralism and criticize unilateral policies, amid growing trade tensions with the United States under the Trump administration. The confirmation follows speculation about a possible Brazilian absence from the summit.

item.title: Crime organizado amplia influência sobre eleições no Brasil
item.description: Organized crime is expanding its influence in Brazilian elections through illicit campaign financing, vote-buying, and voter intimidation in territories under its control. The Electoral Justice and Public Prosecutor’s Office warn of a growing threat to democratic integrity, particularly in areas where criminal groups exercise parallel authority to the state.

item.title: Pesquisas: o impacto do novo tarifaço de Trump na disputa Lula x Flávio
item.description: The new US tariff package may influence the 2026 presidential race between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, according to Murilo Hidalgo of Paraná Pesquisas. While Lula seeks to link Flávio's meeting with Trump to tariff consequences to gain ground, the current impact may be smaller than in past episodes due to the limited scope of the measures. The Banco Master case, which previously harmed Flávio's image, is likely to lose relevance amid the rapid succession of new political events.

item.title: PSB articula candidatura de Datena à Câmara dos Deputados
item.description: The PSB is articulating the candidacy of José Luiz Datena for the Chamber of Deputies in the 2026 elections, with support from Vice President Geraldo Alckmin and Senate pre-candidate Márcio França. Datena, currently host of 'Na Mesa com Datena' on TV Brasil, would have to leave the broadcaster by June 30 if he runs, and his campaign would focus on public security, a topic he emphasizes by stating 'the law is lax in punishing crimes'. His last political attempt was in 2024, when he ran for mayor of São Paulo as a PSDB candidate, becoming known for an act of violence during a debate.

item.title: PL receberá maior fatia do fundo eleitoral em 2026
item.description: The PL will receive the largest share of the Special Campaign Financing Fund (FEFC) in 2026, with 881 million reais, followed by the PT (615 million) and União Brasil (526 million). Distribution follows criteria set by the Elections Law, allocating funds based on equal shares, past electoral performance in the Chamber of Deputies, current representation in the Chamber, and Senate representation. The total distributed is 4.9 billion reais, with the top three parties receiving about 40%.

item.title: ‘Quero radicalizar no centro’, diz Aécio sobre possível pré-candidatura à presidência
item.description: Aécio Neves, national president of the PSDB, advocates for building a center-led presidential candidacy for 2026, rejecting the polarization between Lula and Bolsonaro. He states he is not seeking a personal pre-candidacy but aims to construct a project uniting political forces beyond the extremes, citing talks with figures like Joaquim Barbosa and criticizing the 'vote by rejection' dynamic. Despite polling at 3% with high rejection, Aécio insists he is not yet in campaign mode and wants to offer a moderate alternative focused on reforms and political pacification.

item.title: Pesquisa Atlas: crime organizado amplia pressão sobre Lula
item.description: The AtlasIntel poll indicates that public security, particularly the fight against organized crime, is one of the main political challenges for Lula's government and is expected to be central in the 2026 presidential race. There is high public dissatisfaction with the government's performance in this area, alongside broad support for tougher measures against organized crime.

item.title: Caiado nega chapa conjunta com Zema e diz que ambos manterão pré-candidaturas à Presidência da República
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) denied forming a joint ticket with Romeu Zema (Novo) for the 2026 presidential election, stating both will maintain independent candidacies. He clarified that their talks aimed only to foster cooperation among center-right pre-candidates to avoid fragmentation in the runoff, following a joint event with Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in Belo Horizonte.

item.title: STF retoma ação penal contra ex-presidente da Câmara Eduardo Cunha por corrupção
item.description: The STF has resumed the criminal action against former deputy Eduardo Cunha for corruption, based on the ruling that privileged jurisdiction applies to crimes committed during office, even after mandate loss. The accusation involves undue advantages received from OAS between 2012 and 2014 in exchange for favorable actions benefiting the company in projects such as the privatization of Galeão and Confins airports and BNDES financing for the Arena das Dunas stadium. Cunha, currently a pre-candidate for federal deputy from MG, could benefit from changes to the Clean Record Law that reduce the ineligibility period for 'dirty record' candidates.

item.title: TSE divulga distribuição do Fundo Especial de Financiamento de Campanha para as Eleições 2026
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) announced the distribution of approximately R$ 4.9 billion from the Special Campaign Finance Fund (FEFC) for the 2026 General Elections, allocated to 30 political parties. The funds will be distributed according to legal criteria based on party representation in the National Congress, in compliance with the Elections Law and TSE Resolution No. 23.605/2019.

item.title: As bolhas não têm respostas para a situação geopolítica na qual Trump joga o Brasil
item.description: The article critiques the mistaken belief that Trump could be a strategic ally for Brazil, emphasizing that his interests are purely instrumental: exploiting Brazil as a commodities supplier and pressuring U.S. financial and digital sectors. Both Lula and the Bolsonaro clan are portrayed as equally unprepared to navigate this dynamic — Lula for conflating ideological rhetoric with effective action, and the Bolsonaros for blindly idolizing Trump while ignoring that powers act on interests, not friendship. The absence of a coherent national project leaves Brazil vulnerable to external pressures that force binary choices between the U.S. and China.

item.title: Produtora de Dark Horse contratou advogado de Frias para executar programa com a Prefeitura de SP
item.description: The Conhecer Brazil Institute, linked to the producer of the 'Dark Horse' film about Bolsonaro, hired the lawyer who represented federal deputy Mário Frias in court to execute the Wi-Fi Libre SP program with São Paulo City Hall. The R$108 million contract for installing free internet points in low-income communities is under investigation by São Paulo's Civil Police for suspected diversion of public funds to finance the film, including a R$341,900 payment to the lawyer without service details. City Hall denies irregularities, calling the allegations unfounded speculation.

item.title: Crime organizado se infiltra nas eleições e troca até cocaína por votos
item.description: Organized crime is directly infiltrating Brazilian elections, financing candidates with drug trafficking and robbery proceeds, and coercing voters in territories controlled by groups like PCC, Comando Vermelho and militias. In Rio de Janeiro, the TRE-RJ has already changed the location of 53 polling stations in 2024 and identified 20 zones for relocation in 2026 due to threats and physical intimidation of voters, undermining electoral freedom. Cases such as Sadi Vieira (SC), Michel Maia and Dinho Resenha (RJ) illustrate collusion between state agents, candidates and parallel power structures.

item.title: Aécio se reúne com Joaquim Barbosa por “caminho fora da popularização”
item.description: Aécio Neves (PSDB-MG) met with former Supreme Court Justice Joaquim Barbosa (DC) in Rio de Janeiro to discuss alternatives to political polarization in the 2026 elections. Both are considering building an alternative candidacy, with Barbosa having recently joined the DC party and being seen as a potential presidential candidate. Aécio highlighted Barbosa's electoral recall due to his role in the mensalão trial and as STF president, and said they will monitor polls to assess viability.

item.title: Lula reage a pressão dos EUA e diz que Brasil não adotará postura de “vira-lata”
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized the United States in a social media video, stating that Brazil will not accept a posture of submission before major powers. He emphasized that, in response to potential commercial pressures, the country will expand its international partnerships rather than yield to external demands. Lula reiterated that Brazil has abandoned its 'vira-lata' stance in foreign policy.

item.title: Aliados de Lula vão aos EUA, e Janones diz que faltou humildade ao avaliar relação Bolsonaro-Trump
item.description: Allies of President Lula (PT) arrived in Washington this week to strengthen dialogue with U.S. Democratic lawmakers and promote an alternative narrative to that presented by Bolsonaro’s allies, such as Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and former deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro. The initiative aims to counterbalance the influence of Brazil’s right wing in the United States and reinforce the international image of Lula’s government. Federal Deputy André Janones remarked that there was a lack of humility in assessing the relationship between Bolsonaro and Trump.

item.title: Messias vai à Marcha para Jesus como representante de Lula
item.description: Jorge Messias, Minister of the Attorney General's Office, is attending the March for Jesus in São Paulo as an official representative of the Lula government for the fourth consecutive year. The event marks his first public appearance since his Senate defeat for a Supreme Court seat, bringing together evangelical leaders and politicians from opposing political camps.

item.title: Dino marca julgamento de Eduardo Bolsonaro para 16 de junho
item.description: Brazil's STF First Chamber has scheduled Eduardo Bolsonaro's trial for June 16 over allegations he attempted to interfere in his father's case by lobbying for sanctions against Supreme Court ministers. Relator Alexandre de Moraes deemed the case mature for judgment after final arguments, despite the Public Defender's Office arguing Eduardo lacked effective participation while residing in the U.S. The indictment was filed by the PGR on September 22, 2024, and accepted on November 15, 2025.

item.title: Aécio Neves e Joaquim Barbosa discutem possível chapa para a Presidência em 2026
item.description: Aécio Neves, national president of the PSDB, met with Joaquim Barbosa, former president of the Supreme Federal Court and member of the DC party, to discuss a potential presidential ticket for 2026 as an alternative to the polarization between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. The meeting focused on analyzing the electoral landscape and assessing the viability of a joint candidacy based on future polling. Aécio highlighted Barbosa’s public recognition from the Mensalão trial and emphasized that both seek a path outside Brazil’s dominant political poles.

item.title: Renan Santos e o ministro 'terrivelmente católico' ao STF
item.description: Renan Santos, a political candidate, states he will use a peculiar criterion to choose a minister for the STF, contrasting with Lula's declaration to advocate for evangelical Jorge Messias for the Court. The subscriber-only article highlights this divergence in strategies for naming individuals to the Supreme Federal Court.

item.title: Governo vê espaço para negociar tarifa de 25%, mas não a de 12,5%
item.description: The Brazilian government believes there is room to negotiate a potential 25% additional tariff on exports to the U.S., recommended by the USTR under Section 301, but refuses to reduce the 12.5% tariff, seen as the new normal and applied to multiple countries. Technical talks between Lula and Trump have a June 7 deadline, aiming to delay or avoid the 25% tariff set for July 15, though Brazil acknowledges it must offer concessions, such as adjusting ethanol tariffs, currently at 18% in Brazil versus 2.5% in the U.S.

item.title: Nikolas diz que eleitores de direita são “mais bonitos e cheirosos”
item.description: Federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) stated during a Belo Horizonte Municipal Chamber session that right-wing voters are 'more beautiful and fragrant' than left-wing voters, responding to protests against the honorary citizenship awarded to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ). He labeled left-wing protesters as 'vagrants,' linked them to the PCC and CV criminal factions, and supported their designation as terrorist organizations by the U.S. government. His remarks were met with applause from supporters.

item.title: Aécio Neves e Joaquim Barbosa juntos na eleição?
item.description: Aécio Neves, national president of the PSDB, met with former Supreme Court Justice Joaquim Barbosa to discuss the 2026 electoral landscape. The meeting, held at a bookstore in Rio de Janeiro, aimed to explore the possibility of building an alternative political front outside the dominant poles of the electoral dispute. No formal candidacy or alliance has been confirmed as of yet.

item.title: Romário contraria PL e anuncia voto a favor de PEC pelo fim da escala 6x1
item.description: Senator Romário (PL-RJ) announced he will vote in favor of the PEC to end the 6x1 work schedule, going against the stance of most of his party, which supports an alternative proposal by Senator Rogério Marinho to flexibilize working hours. He had initially signed Marinho’s bill but withdrew his support after concluding the text was widely perceived as harmful to Brazilian workers, stating it made no sense to remain associated with it if the public viewed it negatively. His decision followed pressure from supporters of the government-backed PEC, such as councilman Rick Azevedo, and came after the bolsonarist bloc in the Chamber reversed its position to support the government’s PEC, marking a significant shift from their earlier opposition.

item.title: Renan Santos se aproxima da Faria Lima
item.description: Renan Santos, pre-candidate of Missão ao Planalto, will participate in a meeting with clients of Genial Investimentos on Faria Lima Avenue, signaling his outreach to the financial market. Despite low voter intention polls (2%-3%), he is seen as the leading 'third way' option and ranks third in the Datrix Index for digital performance among presidential candidates, with 19.39 points — behind only Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro.
